task.name: A role whose output is only usable when structured is assigned to a model that cannot produce it, so the gate depending on that output presents no recommendation and cannot say why
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2378
---

**Depends on #2378.** The assignment guard this issue asks for has to consult whether a model has demonstrated it can return a structured result. #2378 is what produces that fact, by exercising the capability and reporting per-capability outcomes instead of a single pass. Without it there is no recorded answer to "can this model return a structured artifact," and this guard would have to re-derive the answer at assignment time or assume it — which is the assumption that caused the failure described here.

## Observed

A story reached the escalate gate. The gate ran its advisor, the advisor produced output, and the
gate then presented its full set of operator actions with no recommendation attached and no
indication that the advisory step had failed rather than declined.

The advisor had been assigned to a model whose transport rejected the structured tool-call request.
The run fell back to plain text, which cannot carry the structured report the gate requires, so
report validation failed and the gate recorded the advisory as unavailable. The advisory step
consumed wall clock and spend and returned nothing usable.

Because there was no recommendation, the expiry path had nothing to apply and preserved the
checkpoint for an operator instead. The story had already been marked failed by then, so the
preserved decision was for work no longer running.

The model carried an explicit eligibility restriction in project configuration naming the phases it
was allowed to serve. That restriction did not prevent this assignment, because the advisor role is
not one of the phases the restriction vocabulary can express.

## Expected

A role whose result is only usable as a structured artifact is assigned only to a model able to
produce that artifact. Where no eligible model can, the role reports that it could not run, and the
step that depends on it states that its input is missing rather than presenting a degraded result as
a complete one. A step that produces nothing usable is not silently indistinguishable from a step
that ran and had nothing to say.

Eligibility declared for a model governs every role that model can be assigned. Where a role sits
outside the vocabulary those declarations use, it is nameable in that vocabulary, so a restriction an
operator writes cannot be silently narrower than the set of jobs the model will actually be given.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom.** The escalate gate offered its operator actions with no advisory recommendation, and the
advisory-unavailable state was reached through a failure rather than an absence of opinion.

**Evidence.**

- `src/theforge/config/model_identity.py:79` — `KNOWN_PHASES` is `frozenset({"preflight", "dev",
  "plan", "review"})`. The advisor role is not a member, so it cannot appear in a
  `routing.phase_eligibility` list.
- `src/theforge/config/model_catalog.py:303` — parsed phases are rejected when outside
  `KNOWN_PHASES`, so an operator cannot name the advisor role even deliberately.
- Run log, escalate gate on one story: the advisor start line, then a transport error on the
  tool-call request and a fallback to single-shot text mode, then
  `advisory report failed validation: ['no <advisory_report> block found in advisor output']`.
- The resulting pending record carries `advisory_unavailable: true` alongside the full options list.

**Ruled out.** Not the advisor prompt: the advisor was reached and produced output. Not the report
validator: it correctly rejected text with no report block. Not the expiry path, which behaved as
specified — it had no recommendation to apply. Not operator configuration error: the restriction the
operator wrote was accepted by config validation and simply does not reach this role.

**Confirmed cause.** Advisor assignment draws from the eligible model set without requiring the
capability its output format depends on, and the eligibility vocabulary cannot express the advisor
role, so neither the automatic path nor an operator override can keep an unsuitable model out of it.

**Affected code path.** Advisor model selection, the tool-call-to-text fallback in the transport
layer, and advisory report validation at the escalate gate.

**Fix-success criterion.** A model that cannot produce the advisor's structured output is not given
the advisor role; when the role cannot be filled, the gate states that the advisory is missing and
why, and that state is distinguishable from an advisor that ran and returned no recommendation.

outcome.message: Preflight: spec is blocked. Spec explicitly depends on issue #2378 to supply a recorded per-capability (structured-output) outcome for each model; no such recording mechanism exists anywhere in the current baseline (only a manual, operator-invoked `forge check-providers` probe in provider_readiness.py, never consulted at runtime). The spec's own fix-success criterion requires assignment to consult that recorded fact rather than assume capability, so it is architecturally unimplementable until #2378 lands.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
